title: The Fall of Jarasandha
body:
The Fall of Jarasandha

मम वत्र्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ।

"In whatever way people surrender unto me, I reciprocate with them accordingly. Everyone follows my path, knowingly or unknowingly, O son of Pritha. (Gita IV-11)"

As the prosperity of Indraprastha reached its zenith, Yudhishthira's advisors and brothers urged him to perform the Rajasuya Yajna to assert his status as Emperor. However, the performance of this grand sacrifice was obstructed by the mighty King Jarasandha of Magadha. Jarasandha was an embodiment of raw material strength and imperial hubris, holding eighty-six independent princes captive in his dungeons, intending to immolate them as human sacrifices to satisfy his ego under the guise of ritual piety.
Shree Krishna advised Yudhishthira that Jarasandha could not be defeated by conventional military legions due to his vast army. Instead, he proposed a stratagem targeting Jarasandha's adherence to the Kshatriya code of honor. Disguising themselves as ascetics who had taken holy vows of silence, Shree Krishna, Bhima, and Arjuna entered Magadha. By choosing to approach Jarasandha at midnight, they played to his custom of receiving holy guests at their convenience.
When Jarasandha questioned their identity—noticing the calluses left on their hands by bowstrings—they threw off their disguises and demanded a duel to the death. Jarasandha accepted, choosing Bhima as his equal in wrestling. The duel raged for fourteen days, showcasing a brutal struggle of physical limbs. It was only when Shree Krishna split a blade of grass in two, throwing the halves in opposite directions, that Bhima understood the secret of Jarasandha's split birth and tore him apart, casting the halves in opposite directions to prevent them from merging. This act demonstrated that mere physical power (bala), without the illuminating wisdom (jnana) of the Supreme, is ultimately self-destructive.
